questions.lo: Cells and organisation: cells, tissues, organs and systems; animal vs plant cells; specialised and unicellular organisms
questions.q: Which THREE parts are found in a plant cell but NOT in an animal cell?
options: Cell wall, permanent vacuole and chloroplasts
questions.explain: Plant cells contain everything an animal cell has, PLUS three extras: a cellulose cell wall, a permanent vacuole and chloroplasts. Nucleus, cytoplasm, membrane and mitochondria are found in both.

questions.lo: Cells and organisation: cells, tissues, organs and systems; animal vs plant cells; specialised and unicellular organisms
questions.q: Put these in order from smallest to largest level of organisation.
questions.explain: Cells are the fundamental unit. Groups of similar cells form a tissue, several tissues form an organ, and organs working together form an organ system.

questions.lo: Cells and organisation: cells, tissues, organs and systems; animal vs plant cells; specialised and unicellular organisms
questions.q: A red blood cell has no nucleus and a dimpled disc shape. Which job is this structure best adapted for?
options: Carrying as much oxygen as possible
questions.explain: Losing the nucleus and having a dimpled disc shape lets a red blood cell pack in more haemoglobin and have a bigger surface area, so it carries more oxygen — a clear example of structure fitting function.

questions.lo: The skeletal and muscular systems: support, protection, movement, joints and antagonistic muscles
questions.q: Which of these is NOT one of the main functions of the human skeleton?
questions.explain: The skeleton provides support, protects organs, allows movement (as levers) and makes blood cells in the bone marrow. Digestive enzymes are made by organs like the pancreas, not by bones.

questions.lo: The skeletal and muscular systems: support, protection, movement, joints and antagonistic muscles
questions.q: You bend your arm at the elbow to lift a bag. What are the biceps and triceps doing?
options: Both contract at the same time
Both relax at the same time
questions.explain: Muscles can only pull. To bend the arm the biceps contracts and pulls the forearm up, while its antagonistic partner the triceps relaxes. To straighten the arm they swap over.

questions.lo: The skeletal and muscular systems: support, protection, movement, joints and antagonistic muscles
questions.q: Why are muscles arranged in antagonistic pairs?
options: Because muscles can only pull, not push
Because one muscle is stronger than the other
Because bones cannot bend on their own
Because muscles need to rest all the time
questions.explain: A muscle can only shorten (contract) to pull a bone; it cannot push. So a second muscle is needed to pull the bone back the other way — this opposite pairing is called antagonistic.

questions.lo: Nutrition and digestion: balanced diet, food tests, the digestive system, enzymes and gut bacteria
questions.q: Which nutrient group is mainly needed for growth and repair of the body?
questions.explain: Proteins are used for growth and repair. Carbohydrates and lipids are mainly energy, and fibre keeps food moving through the gut.

questions.lo: Nutrition and digestion: balanced diet, food tests, the digestive system, enzymes and gut bacteria
questions.q: A student adds iodine solution to some bread and it turns blue-black. What does the bread contain?
questions.explain: Iodine turns from orange-brown to blue-black when starch is present. The colour change is the positive result of the starch test.

questions.lo: Nutrition and digestion: balanced diet, food tests, the digestive system, enzymes and gut bacteria
questions.q: In which organ is most digested food absorbed into the blood?
questions.explain: The small intestine is where soluble digested food molecules are absorbed into the blood. The large intestine mainly absorbs water, and the stomach churns and starts digestion.

questions.lo: Nutrition and digestion: balanced diet, food tests, the digestive system, enzymes and gut bacteria
questions.q: Which statement about digestive enzymes is correct?
options: They are living microbes that eat food
They are protein molecules that act as biological catalysts
They are a type of vitamin
They are only found in plants
questions.explain: Enzymes are protein molecules made by cells that act as biological catalysts, speeding up the breakdown of food. They are NOT alive, so they cannot 'die' — but very high temperatures or the wrong pH can denature them.

questions.lo: Nutrition and digestion: balanced diet, food tests, the digestive system, enzymes and gut bacteria
questions.q: What is one useful role of bacteria that live in the human digestive system?
options: They help digest food and make some vitamins
They replace the need for a balanced diet
They absorb oxygen for the body
questions.explain: Helpful gut bacteria assist with digesting food, make some vitamins and crowd out harmful microbes. Not all bacteria are harmful.

questions.lo: Gas exchange systems: lungs, breathing mechanism and alveoli
questions.q: Where in the lungs does gas exchange between air and blood take place?
questions.explain: The alveoli are tiny air sacs with a huge surface area, thin walls and a rich blood supply — ideal for oxygen to pass into the blood and carbon dioxide to pass out.

questions.lo: Gas exchange systems: lungs, breathing mechanism and alveoli
questions.q: When you breathe IN, what happens to make air enter the lungs?
options: The diaphragm and rib muscles contract, so the chest gets bigger and pressure inside drops
The diaphragm relaxes and the chest gets smaller
Air is pushed in by the heart pumping
questions.explain: Breathing in: the diaphragm and rib muscles contract, the chest volume increases, the pressure inside falls below outside pressure, so air is pushed in. Breathing out is the reverse.

questions.lo: Gas exchange systems: lungs, breathing mechanism and alveoli
questions.q: Which statement correctly describes the difference between breathing and respiration?
options: They are two words for exactly the same thing
Breathing moves air in and out; respiration is the reaction in cells that releases energy
Breathing happens in cells; respiration happens in the lungs
Respiration only happens when you are asleep
questions.explain: Breathing is a muscular action moving air in and out of the lungs. Respiration is a chemical reaction inside every cell that releases energy from glucose using oxygen. Breathing simply supplies that oxygen — they are not the same thing.

questions.lo: Reproduction: human reproductive system, gametes, menstrual cycle, gestation and plant pollination
questions.q: What are the male and female gametes in humans?
questions.explain: In humans the male gamete is the sperm (made in the testes) and the female gamete is the egg or ovum (made in the ovaries). Pollen and ovules are plant gametes.

questions.lo: Reproduction: human reproductive system, gametes, menstrual cycle, gestation and plant pollination
questions.q: What is pollination in flowering plants?
options: The joining of an egg and a sperm
The transfer of pollen from an anther to a stigma
The growth of a seed into a new plant
The building up of the uterus lining
questions.explain: Pollination is the transfer of pollen from the anther (male part) to the stigma (female part), carried by insects or wind. Fertilisation, which forms seeds, happens afterwards.

questions.lo: Reproduction: human reproductive system, gametes, menstrual cycle, gestation and plant pollination
questions.q: During pregnancy, how does a developing baby receive food and oxygen from its mother?
options: It does not need any until birth
questions.explain: The placenta lets food and oxygen pass from the mother's blood to the baby. This is also why harmful substances from smoking or alcohol can reach and harm the foetus.

questions.lo: Health: effects of diet, exercise, drugs and smoking on the body
questions.q: Smoking damages the alveoli. Why is this a problem for the whole body?
options: It stops the heart from beating completely
Less oxygen can pass into the blood, so cells get less oxygen for respiration
It means the person no longer needs to eat
It makes bones grow too quickly
questions.explain: Damaged alveoli have a smaller surface area for gas exchange, so less oxygen enters the blood. The body's cells then get less oxygen for respiration, leaving the person short of breath and with less energy.

questions.lo: Health: effects of diet, exercise, drugs and smoking on the body
questions.q: Which lifestyle choice is most likely to keep the heart, muscles and skeleton healthy?
options: Eating a balanced diet and exercising regularly
Eating far more energy than the body uses
questions.explain: A balanced diet and regular exercise keep body systems working well and help control body mass. Too much energy in the diet can lead to obesity, and smoking harms the body.
